narrative:
The model predicts that you have a 12% chance of failing your final year, which indicates a significant risk of not passing. This prediction is based on several factors that have been shown to influence student outcomes.

The most important factor in your case is the amount of time you dedicate to studying each week. Compared to many students who passed, your study time falls within the 5-10 hours range, which is less than the average of 2-5 hours for those who succeeded. This suggests that increasing your study time could greatly enhance your chances of passing.

Another critical aspect is your history of past failures. While you have not failed any classes before, the model indicates that students with a similar profile who have struggled in the past tend to face challenges in their final year. This could mean that maintaining a strong performance throughout the year is essential for you.

Lastly, the reason you chose this school—primarily for its proximity to home—also plays a role. Many students who selected their school based on reputation or course offerings tend to perform better. This suggests that aligning your educational environment with your academic goals could be beneficial.

To improve your academic performance, consider increasing your study hours, seeking additional support if needed, and reflecting on your motivations for choosing this school. Engaging more deeply with your studies and utilizing available resources can help you turn this prediction around.
